chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: Oldest brother William, pianist at the movie house
summary: His eldest brother was a fine pianist who taught the others, and played silent films at the Earl Theater on South Street while William and Floyd gigged in small clubs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: In the city itself. Early on -- in the early life, my oldest brother was into the music business. He was a very fine pianist. And I guess that's where we got our education -- you know, experience from him, (inaudible) get into the music business. He taught us all, (inaudible) down the

line -- Bob, you know, from one to the other. My oldest brother was William McRae and Floyd McRae. They were the first to (inaudible). They were playing around Philly clubs, like that.
You remember any of the clubs that they played?
Well, no. Just like little small clubs, (inaudible) gigging around Philly.

My oldest brother was like -- he would study. He was (inaudible) like a concert pianist, and he worked a couple of movie houses back in those days, I want to say. They didn't have, you know, the silent movies, and he used to play the Earl Theater on South Street. we used to go (inaudible) watch him play the piano -- play all these -- you know, one time western and country. Story of the cowboys, story of -- (inaudible). Comedy things, yes.
Comedy things (inaudible) just playing the piano and all that kind of stuff.
Keystone Cops and that sort of thing.
